18	The bulk of Plaintiffs’ breach claim centers around their argument that TD’s conduct violated the NACHA Rules, which Plaintiffs claim were incorporated into the Account Agreement. See Compl. at ¶ 166-67. In order to address this claim we must first determine whether the NACHA rules were in fact incorporated. In support of this point, Plaintiffs cite to page 16 of the Account Agreement, which states in relevant part:
19	International ACH and Wire Transactions
20	If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved....

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"The insuring clause is a short promise to pay proceeds 'according to the following provisions'; the text as reproduced is garbled but the operative promise is conventional and does not name any indeterminate term.","reasoning_cat2":"It simply subordinates itself to Sections 3-10 (e.g. 4.1 Payment of Proceeds), so it harmonises rather than conflicts.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"A standard 20-day free-look with a refund of 'any premium you have paid'; the wording is corrupted in transcription but the mechanism (return within 20 days, void from the beginning) is definite.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits comfortably with 3.1 (premium payable at or before delivery) and 7.2 (effective date); no competing provision addresses rescission.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"The paid-up benefit is stated only in fragments — 'level amount based on: a. The current Policy Account Value less any Policy Indebtedness' — so the actual amount of paid-up insurance and the triggering birthday are left indeterminate on the face of the clause.","reasoning_cat2":"It has to be reconciled with 4.2 (death benefit tied to Specified Amount and Coverage Option) and with the Maturity Date in Section 1, and the relationship between an automatic paid-up conversion and continuing Monthly Insurance Charges under 5.3/5.10 is not spelled out.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"An introductory statement that definitions are subordinate to the fuller description in Sections 3-10; 'more complete description' is loose but nothing operative turns on it alone.","reasoning_cat2":"It functions as an internal priority rule, so where a Section 2 definition diverges from an operative section (e.g. 2.15 vs 5.3) this clause is what a court would use to harmonise them.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line definition identifying the Insured as the person listed in Section 1 whose death causes proceeds to be paid; the transcription is broken but the concept is unambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2.2 (Owner may be someone other than the Insured) and 4.1; no tension found.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"'You or Your' means the Owner, expressly allowing the Owner to differ from the Insured; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches 8.1-8.3 ownership provisions and Section 1's designation of the same person as Owner and Insured; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"'We or Us' identifies the insurer; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Used consistently throughout Sections 3-10; no inconsistency.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"The definition breaks off after 'as named in the original [application] but may subsequently be changed as provided', so as reproduced it does not complete the change mechanism.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be read with 8.4, which adds that the Owner is beneficiary if none is named and deals with predeceasing beneficiaries; the definition alone is incomplete rather than contradictory.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"'Proceeds' is defined as the total amount payable on death or on surrender, a definite two-branch definition cross-referencing Section 4.","reasoning_cat2":"4.1 pays 'Surrender Value' on surrender and 'Death Proceeds' on death, and 9.4 deducts indebtedness from 'Policy Proceeds'; the several proceeds labels are close but not obviously inconsistent.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"Policy Date is the computation anchor shown in Section 1; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2.17 (Monthly Due Date same day as Policy Date) and 7.2 (effect on later of Policy Date or premium payment).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"'The date coverage commences' is a short definition that defers to Section 7.2, 6.2 and riders; the reference to '% 2' is a transcription artefact rather than a naming of a genuinely ambiguous term.","reasoning_cat2":"3.1 says there is no coverage until premium is paid while 7.2 sets effect on the later of Policy Date or payment; the definition points to 7.2 and largely harmonises, but the interplay with the Temporary Insurance Agreement is left open.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c012","reasoning_cat1":"Only a fragment survives — 'upon the Insured's age on the birthday nearest the first' — so the age convention (age nearest birthday as of what date) cannot be applied from the clause itself.","reasoning_cat2":"Age drives the 5.4 Cost of Insurance table and the 4.2 risk-percentage corridor, so an incomplete age definition has real downstream consequences, though no direct contradiction appears.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c013","reasoning_cat1":"The clause says premium amount and frequency are what the Owner 'most recently elect[s]' yet also that during the first two Policy years the Section 1 figure 'is the minimum that must be paid' — a flexible-premium description carrying a mandatory floor.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be reconciled with 3.2(1)-(2) (same two-year minimum expressed differently) and with 5.10's no-lapse guarantee keyed to one-twelfth of the Planned Periodic Premium; the three formulations are similar but not identical.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"A short definition requiring the Minimum Initial Premium before delivery, with the amount left to Section 1; definite in structure.","reasoning_cat2":"3.1 says it must be paid 'at or before' delivery and 7.2 makes the effective date turn on payment; 'before' versus 'at or before' is a slight but real divergence.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c015","reasoning_cat1":"The definition is truncated mid-sentence, leaving 'the amount you specified in the original application' and the increase/decrease right without their qualifying words.","reasoning_cat2":"6.2 supplies the change conditions and 5.9 reduces the Specified Amount on withdrawal under Option A; the definition defers to those and does not contradict them.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c016","reasoning_cat1":"Death Benefit is defined as the amount payable 'prior to any adjustment specified in Section 4', depending on Specified Amount and Coverage Option; the deferral is clear even though the text is corrupted.","reasoning_cat2":"Squares with 4.2's greater-of formulas and with 4.2's later adjustments for riders and indebtedness; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c017","reasoning_cat1":"'Both coverage options provide for an increased death benefit when the difference between the Policy Account Value and the death benefit reaches a minimum size' uses the undefined and vague phrase 'a minimum size'.","reasoning_cat2":"The corridor is actually implemented by the risk-percentage table in 4.2, so the definition's loose phrase is filled in there; the fit is workable but the definition overstates its own generality.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.17},
